units: metre (model coordinates are metres; source STEP was millimetres, scaled by 0.001)
up_axis: +Y (base plate lies in XZ plane, its top face at y=0.020 m, gimbal rises along +Y)
coordinate_frame: right-handed, same axes as the STEP file; origin at the underside-centre of XY Base Plate

x_axis.how: xgroup.rotation.x = angle (radians). Node origin = pivot, children have the inverse pivot baked in. Axis measured from the cylinder axes of X Shaft / X Spindle / eRob110 / X Shaft Housing: all exactly +X through (y=0.200 m, z=0).

y_axis.how: The physical Y axis (cylinder axes of Y Shaft / Y Spindle / eRob90 / Y housings) is +Z tilted by 1.180 deg about X (direction (0,0.020599,0.999788) in XGROUP frame). That tilt is baked into the YGROUP node rotation (Euler XYZ = (-0.02060,0,0)); keep rotation.x/.y as loaded and set ONLY ygroup.rotation.z = angle (Euler order XYZ, three.js default) to rotate exactly about the physical axis. If you ignore the tilt and overwrite rotation, error is 1.18 deg.

beam_direction_detail: Reflector is a concave dish opening toward +Y (rim plane normal (0.026,0.999,-0.020) in world at zero angles, i.e. ~1.2 deg from +Y; fitted paraboloid axis ~+Y). At zero angles the face points straight UP (vertical, perpendicular to the BASE plate). Geometric boresight/rim normal [0.026,0.9994,-0.020]. Feed is displaced in +X (~0.30 m off the dish axis at x~0.35 m, y~1.33-1.45 m), so the real RF beam of an off-axis feed may be squinted toward -X.
notes: Grouping deviates from the brief on purpose where geometry says so: X Fork Arm Front/Back and the X Shaft/X Spindle stubs, the X-side Donut Support and cable gland are BASE (arms are bolted upright on the XY Base Plate with identical footprint; shaft/spindle stubs are flush against the arm inner faces and sit coaxially inside the box bearings). The X motor eRob110 and Y motor eRob90 bodies are in XGROUP (inside the gimbal box). Because motor, shafts, spindles are all coaxial with the rotation axis, rotating them with or without the box is visually indistinguishable.
Y Shaft, Y Spindle, the Y-side Donut Support are in YGROUP (they attach to the Y-Dish Arms which carry the dish); Y Shaft Housing and both UCFCX08 bearing housings are XGROUP.
Colours: every solid in the STEP carries the same SolidWorks colour (0.591,0.638,0.855) except 6 parts default grey (0.6,0.6,0.62); per-part colours are preserved but are essentially uniform.

Many sub-assembly parts have Chinese names that the STEP stores with non-ASCII characters collapsed to underscores; those node names look like "____MA100B...", suffixed with [NAUOxx] when not unique. extras.step_name keeps the raw name.
Mesh: linear deflection <= 0.6 mm (0.004 x diag for small parts, min 0.05 mm), angular 0.5 rad (0.9 rad for parts < 80 mm); eRob motors 2.0 mm. No parts were dropped.

Dish swing: rotating XGROUP about the pivot at y=0.2 m swings the 1.1 m dish / 1.45 m tall feed through a large radius (clearance with the base plate/fork arms is not modelled; the dish sweeps y 0.5-1.45 m from the pivot).
Normals are int8 normalized (KHR_mesh_quantization-free, standard BYTE normalized VEC3, stride 4).
